observation_summary: The FastDateFormat 'z' pattern incorrectly prints the system's default timezone name instead of the timezone associated with the Calendar instance being formatted.
reasoning_summary: The fix involved changing the internal logic of the TimeZoneNameRule class. Instead of relying on a pre-cached TimeZone instance (which was incorrectly capturing the system default or the printer's default), the code was updated to dynamically retrieve the TimeZone from the Calendar object passed to the appendTo method. This is a correction of the computational procedure used to determine the timezone display name, fitting the Algorithm/Method category.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'TimeZoneNameRule class stopped respecting the Calendar instance's timezone, and instead now always uses the mTimeZone of the FastDateFormat instance itself'
The fix diff shows the removal of the 'zone' field from the TimeZoneNameRule class and the addition of 'TimeZone zone = calendar.getTimeZone();' inside the appendTo method.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves changing how a variable is initialized, the root cause is the procedural logic of how the timezone is resolved during the formatting process, not just an incorrect initial value.
The fix does not change the method signature or the contract between components; it changes the internal implementation of how the printer retrieves the timezone information.
